newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASKETBALL-ALBA ADVANCE AFTER NARROW WIN OVER MOSCOW.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-ALBA ADVANCE AFTER NARROW WIN OVER MOSCOW.

text.p: Alba Berlin scored a thrilling 78-76 come-from-behind victory over CSKA Moscow in a EuroLeague basketball game in Berlin on Thursday that assured the German team a spot in the last 16 of the competition.
CSKA, third in last season's Final Four, now look in grave danger of exiting at the group stage.

Berlin's Wendell Alexis scored three three-point baskets in the final four minutes to rescue the home team from a seven-point deficit and Henrik Roedl converted two free throws with 17 seconds left to seal the victory.

Alba, who now have nine wins and six losses in group E, had already defeated CSKA in Moscow by two points but had a surprisingly hard time on its home court before a boisterous sell-out crowd of 9,000 in Max Schmeling arena.

Alexis led Berlin's scorers with 23 points, including 15 in the second half, and guard Sasa Obradovic added 17. Moscow, who have slipped to 7-9 in the group, were led by Valery Dayneko with 25 points and centre Marcus Webb who scored 16 points.

After Roedl's two free throws made it 78-76, Moscow's Sergei Panov was fouled driving to the basket with five seconds left. But Panov missed both shots. The rebound from the second shot was volleyed around before Andrei Kornev grabbed the ball near mid-court. His desperation heave just missed the rim.

Obradovic, the Berlin guard and Yugoslav national team player, spent much of the second half in foul trouble and watched from the bench as Berlin fell behind by seven points midway through the period.
With five minutes to play, he returned to the floor and immediately sparked a rally that brought Berlin back with a three-point shot and driving layup that brought the crowd alive.

The first half had ended level at 39-39. Alba had opened an early 12-4 lead after a pair of three-point shots from Obradovic. But Alba's offensive game began to sputter and CSKA Moscow evened the score at 28-28 with six minutes to play in the first half.

Dayneko scored a team-leading 17 points in the first half with deadly long-range shooting that repeatedly silenced Berlin's huge hometown crowd. As a team, Moscow connected on an impressive 70 percent of their two-point shots compared to 43 percent for Berlin.

CSKA Moscow opened a 55-47 lead midway through the second half after their powerful 206-cm centre Webb muscled his way free under the basket for four straight rim-rattling slam dunks and spearhead a 16-8 run for the visitors.
